answer: A port town cannot trust every ship that docks at its wharf, so it demands proof before granting a berth. An agent economy can do the same with bonded deposits: each identity stakes real funds, like a merchant putting up timber and marble as collateral, and the stake is slashed if the identity misbehaves. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of deposits, so a Sybil attack becomes expensive while honest agents keep operating cheaply.
